decisions.reason: As an organic line extension in a mainstream ham format, it fits the firm's stated direction and can be kept at relatively low incremental cost while supporting the broader organic range.
This organic Kasseler variant is close to the core assortment and likely inexpensive to continue, so a large incumbent would usually retain it unless sales were clearly weak.
Organic pepper salami combines a familiar product type with the firm's organic expansion, making it a reasonably attractive option to keep open in the portfolio.

The teriyaki aspic beef specialty looks like a narrow experimental counter product, and after several years its market value should be sufficiently revealed to justify exit if it has not clearly succeeded.
Fennel-flavoured sliced salami is a more niche taste extension, and in a medium-width portfolio a German meat producer would likely redeploy capacity if demand remained uncertain or limited.
A liver pâté with veal is a traditional premium deli extension close to existing know-how, so the firm has reason to keep it unless performance has been distinctly disappointing.
